evals.prompt:
Review this Go HTTP handler that proxies requests to internal services:

```go
func proxyHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    targetURL := r.URL.Query().Get("url")
    resp, err := http.Get(targetURL)
    if err != nil {
        http.Error(w, err.Error(), 500)
        return
    }
    defer resp.Body.Close()
    body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
    w.Header().Set("Content-Type", resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
    w.Write(body)
}
```
evals.expected_output: Identifies SSRF as the primary vulnerability, plus error message information leakage, missing authentication, unbounded response body reading, and content-type passthrough risks. Each finding maps to OWASP categories.
expectations: Identifies SSRF as the primary/critical vulnerability and references A10
Recommends URL allowlisting (domains and/or protocols) to prevent SSRF
Recommends blocking private/internal IP ranges (127.0.0.0/8, 10.0.0.0/8, etc.)
Identifies error message information leakage (raw error returned to client)
Identifies missing authentication or authorization on the proxy endpoint
Identifies unbounded io.ReadAll as a potential denial-of-service vector
Provides specific code-level fixes, not just abstract guidance
